learning: Lead 0.05 to 0.07 m gave +8.1 score, driven by the oval. The s-bend progress stayed at 0.16 across both leads, so it is not sensing-limited. If the oval keeps improving and the slalom oscillation stays flat, the remaining limit is controller gain or speed.
notes: Lead-only test at y = 0.08 m, the maximum allowed. The controller matches iteration 2 so any change is attributable to lead. Watch steering_oscillation on the slalom for overshoot.
rationale: Iteration 2 (sensor lead y = 0.07 m) raised the score from 52.3 to 60.4. The oval gained most: progress rose from 0.112 to 0.168, rms_error fell from 0.029 to 0.019, and control_effort fell from 1.35 to 0.88. The slalom and s-bend did not move. Both still end off track at about 0.061-0.069 m max_error, against the 0.06 m limit. The s-bend progress was 0.16 at both lead 0.05 m and lead 0.07 m, so lead is not what limits it. Lead is the one geometry lever with a measured, monotonic gain, so this iteration tests lead y = 0.08 m, the top of the allowed range. Geometry changes only in the lead (body 0.18 x 0.12 m, mass 0.6 kg, track 0.10 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, 12 mm sensors at 15 mm spacing). The controller is kept identical to iteration 2 so the lead effect is isolated. Sensor weights are unchanged. The signal magnitude is the same at any lead, because the sensors keep their lateral positions. Only the timing of the correction changes. The main risk is slalom overshoot, which the observation request will show through steering_oscillation. I expect the oval to improve further, and I expect the s-bend and slalom to stay limited by gain or speed rather than by sensing.
